home.head.title1: OpenWalkieTalkie — The open-source handheld radio for your AI agents.
home.head.meta-content1: OpenWalkieTalkie is an open handheld for people who run several AI agents at once: a 480×480 touch screen that shows who needs you, a scroll wheel, and a push-to-talk key that sends your voice to the agent that does. Open hardware, open firmware, open host.
home.head.meta-content2: A palm-sized deck with a touch screen, a scroll wheel and a push-to-talk key. It shows which agent needs you, and your voice goes to the one that does. Open hardware, firmware and host.
home.head.meta-content3: An OpenWalkieTalkie prototype standing on a desk with its screen lit, next to the words Open Walkie Talkie, the open-source handheld radio for your AI agents.
home.head.meta-content4: A deck that shows which agent needs you. Hold PTT and talk to it. Open hardware, firmware and host.

home.features.p2: The screen is the status board. PTT is the radio. The buttons are the decisions. Read the conversation, see who needs you, and respond from the deck.
home.featPtt.button-aria-label1: Push-to-talk demo — hold the button, or hold Space, to talk
home.features.p4: Hold the key from a work face and the screen becomes a LISTENING overlay. Release it and the transcript stays visible while recognition finishes. The deck's microphone streams to your Mac, the words land in the active agent as its next prompt, and the reply can be spoken back through the deck's speaker.
home.featPttReadout.p1: At rest. Hold the key to open a session.
home.featPttOut.div1: The deck's screen while you hold PTT
home.features.p5: Every agent is a channel. A red dot is a question, green is ready, blue is working. Questions sort to the top, so the row you see first is the one that needs you.
home.features.p7: A permission request or a multiple-choice question becomes a card. Scroll to a choice and press ENTER, tap it, or answer by voice. Only a person can approve a Claude Code or Codex permission card.
home.features.p9: One detent, one row. Hold SHIFT and the same wheel slides between faces: Agents, Omarchy, Macropad, Usage, System and Arcade. Double-tap SHIFT to reorder them.
home.features.p11: Nine keys on the touch screen, each with a label and a keystroke. The host posts the chord to your desktop. Edit a key on the deck itself and dictate its label with PTT.
home.features.p13: Your Claude and Codex rate-limit windows as bars, with the active account and countdown to each reset. The host reads them with the logins you already have, nothing else.
home.features.p15: Plug in over USB-C and the host writes a report in under a millisecond. Unplug and the same link, voice included, rides Bluetooth LE. The host takes the cable whenever it is there.
home.demo.p3: Pick a mode. Tap or turn the wheel.

home.blueprint.p2: Build your own from the open designs, or join the waitlist for a finished device. The board, firmware, host service and wire protocol are all in one tree.
home.blueprint.li2: The board, firmware and Mac app, together. Clone it and go.
home.blueprint.li4: The main board, Rev B: a KiCad project with Gerbers, BOM and pick-and-place. CERN-OHL-P 2.0.
home.blueprint.li6: Where it started: CoHDL schematic sources, four fabricated releases, the case CAD.
home.blueprint.li8: Rust firmware on embassy: the faces, the HID link over BLE and USB, the bond journal, power.
home.blueprint.li10: The RT-Thread image with Bluetooth audio, mounting the same UI core.
home.blueprint.li12: deckd and the Mac app, Rust + gpui: the link, the Claude Code and Codex adapters, voice, the open API.
home.blueprint.li14: The wire contract on channel 5. Read it and your script is an agent on the deck.
home.blueprint.p3: Software under MIT. The board, the case and every design file under the permissive CERN Open Hardware Licence. Build it, modify it, sell it, no permission required.
home.blueprint.p4: The hardware design started in CoHDL. The Rev A schematics are source code in the open-source hardware language at cohdl.org, checked by its compiler; Rev B is hand-placed and routed in KiCad from that lineage.
home.blueprint.a-aria-label1: Join the Discord — CoHDL and OpenWalkieTalkie community
home.blueprint.p5: The Mac app includes deckd, automatic app updates, and firmware updates for Rev A and Rev B. The source includes the tools for an initial USB-C or UART flash.

home.download.p2: v0.17.0 for macOS 13 and later, signed and notarized: the companion app for your deck, on Mac, Windows and Omarchy. Windows 10 and 11 as an unsigned preview.
home.download.p3: Open the disk image, drag OpenWalkieTalkie into Applications, then follow the setup in the app. Choose Apple Silicon for an M-series Mac, or Intel for an Intel Mac.
home.download.p4: On Windows 10 or 11 (x64), the unsigned preview supports voice, Claude Code, Codex CLI and Grok Bot. Read the Windows install guide for setup and SmartScreen, and check the preview’s release notes and checksum.
home.download.p5: On an Omarchy (Hyprland) laptop, the service and the Omarchy bridge are built from source: follow the Omarchy guide for the desktop remote, your agent sessions and voice orders.
home.download.p6: The app includes automatic updates and board-aware USB firmware updates for Rev A and Rev B. Initial flashing requires a compatible bootloader. Release notes, firmware & checksums →
